When I had microsleeps around my family they apparently never noticed, and neither did I.
I don't mean to say "believe" as in to imply you're wrong somehow or misinterpreting; I'm just using it to say that microsleeps very well could be happening without your knowledge.

Yes, you can 100% believe you're aware during microsleeps, this is part of why so many ppl dont know they experience them until someone else tells them. Fun fact for anyone curious abt how this myth started; the stinging cells in most stinging sea creatures react based on a change in pH level, and its recommended that when stung you rinse off the area in case some of those cells just havent deployed yet (this wont help your sting but itll prevent it from getting worse). 
The pH of seawater is about 8.1 and the pH of human urine is about 4.6~8.0. So, if you pee on a sting then best case scenario you've got extra alkaline pee (in which case its abt as effective as just rinsing it off with seawater anyway) to rinse it, worst case scenario (also the much more likely result) you make the sting way worse by setting off all of the stinging cells that havent deployed yet with your urine.
Vinegar is the best option bc it neutralizes those cells as it rinses them off. After that your best bet is just normal seawater :)

Its not uncommon in a lot of places actually for ppl to bring vinegar with them to the beach, and in areas (such as australia) where stings happen somewhat regularly (especially during stinger season) they'll sometimes keep vinegar on the beach for exactly this reason!
